## Features

| Feature | Supported |
|---------|-----------|
| Motor control | Back, feet, waist, neck, separate lifts or storage lift, by model |
| Position feedback | ❌ |
| Memory | Two slots, recall and save, on models that have them |
| Presets | ZZ (anti-snore), TV and zero gravity on some models |
| Massage | Vibration; sonic massage up and down on AS models; sonic zones, modes and level on I/HI models |
| Lighting | On/off on P1, toggle on P2, RGB and brightness on RGB layouts |
| Split sides | Five models, from one receiver; on P1 models both sides share the foot motor |
| Bed sensors | Per side: in bed, asleep, heart rate, breathing and snoring (as the bed reports them, without units) |

## Choosing a profile

Choose **CheersSleep app**, then the exact model and its number (the key). The
model's app screen decides whether the bed uses P1 or P2. Notifications that
report the bed's manufacturer data are handled the same way for both formats.
No Bluetooth name rule or PIN is used.

<!-- generated:cheerssleep-profiles -->
<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_codec_docs.py from the codec and profile data. Edit those, not this block. -->

| Format | Movement | Release | Tap burst | Startup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | One frame; the hold is latched for up to 10 s | STOP for the same motor 120 ms after release | One write | Pages Two and Two1: up to 20 address queries, each after a 120 ms wait |
| P2 | Repeats every 100 ms while held, within the hold limit | Zero key at once, for both sides | Command at 0, 100 and 200 ms; release at 300, 400, 500 and 500 ms; an interrupted tap keeps its counter | Simple pages send a B0 query; pages with navigation send a D0 query for side 0 when the parent page resumes or a destination opens |

### Aliases

There are no alternate integration bed-type aliases. Same-page catalog keys are retained individually.

## Wire codec

### Transports

<!-- generated:cheerssleep-transports -->
<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_codec_docs.py from the codec and profile data. Edit those, not this block. -->

| Role | Service | Characteristic |
|---|---|---|
| Write | `6e403587-b5a3-f393-e0a9-e50e24dcca9e` | `6e403588-b5a3-f393-e0a9-e50e24dcca9e` |
| Notify | `6e403587-b5a3-f393-e0a9-e50e24dcca9e` | `6e403589-b5a3-f393-e0a9-e50e24dcca9e` |
<!-- /generated -->

### Framing and checksum

P1 frames are eight bytes: the low byte of a serial number, the PID, a
little-endian 16-bit command and a little-endian 32-bit parameter. The command
counter starts at 1. Ordinary sends increment it before sending, held sends
increment it only when the held command changes, and sleep-module address
queries increment it after sending. Settings use a separate counter that
increments after sending.

P2 frames, in order:

| Frame | Bytes |
|---|---|
| Normal command | `EE`, type 1, length 5, a big-endian 32-bit key, the side, `C0` |
| Setting | `EE`, type 2, an opcode and three value bytes, `C0` |
| Query | `B0` or `D0`, length 1 |

Side 1 is sent as `AA`, side 2 as `BB`, and any other side as its low byte.
Neither format has a checksum, encryption or authentication.

### Write mode

The app keeps Android's default write mode. The integration writes with
response and needs the write property on the exact service and characteristic.
Bleak turns on notifications; the app's extra local registration does not add
a second subscription.

P1 split models use these commands:

| Action | Left | Right |
|---|---|---|
| Memory recall | 6530, 6531 | 6538, 6539 |
| Memory save | 6540, 6541 | 6548, 6549 |
| ZZ, TV, zero gravity | 6511 to 6513 | 6521 to 6523 |

Flat is shared by both sides. P2 memory saves use selectors 5 and 6, followed by
the setting release (`AA`), not the memory recall key.

P1 massage keeps its head and foot levels and the wave mode in the
integration. Steady levels wrap round through off; wave levels wrap from 3 back
to 1. Turning wave mode on sets both levels to 1, and off resets both. The right
head wave intensity 2 command is `0x2401`, an irregular value the app ships and
the integration sends unchanged. P2 massage buttons step the bed's own state,
and the B0 reply reports the levels and mode.

RGB colour, brightness and sonic level settings always use side 0, also on
split models. Sonic zone and mode buttons on the position page keep their
selected side. Colour uses setting 5, brightness setting 10 and sonic level
setting 11, each followed by the setting release (`AA`). AS models change the
sonic level with channel 2 (down and up) and a normal held release to both
sides; their sonic toggle uses parameter 3. I/HI models set an absolute sonic
level with channel 3.

### Responses

| P1 reply | Meaning |
|---|---|
| PID 89 | Sleep-module address in bytes 2 to 7 |
| PID 87 / 88 | Left / right sleep report. Byte 2 holds the snore, in-bed and asleep flags; heart rate, breath rate and the other fields are signed bytes. With nobody in bed, heart and breath rate are 0 |

Replies that are too short are ignored.

A B0 reply needs ten bytes. Byte 9 is the light and is applied before the side
and mode checks. The massage mode is byte 6 minus 1, accepted only from 0 to 2;
bytes 7 and 8 are the signed head and foot levels. NewNine applies only the
massage fields to the selected side. Pages with only a light never gain
massage controls.

A D0 reply needs seventeen bytes:

| Byte | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 4 to 6 | RGB colour (unsigned) |
| 7 | Brightness (signed) |
| 8 | Position-page light on AS models; bit 0 is the shared control mode |
| 11 | Sonic level on I/HI models (signed, clamped to 0 to 100) |
| 12 | Mode (Position500i: the side's low or high nibble) |
| 16 | Light on I/HI models, and the colour-page light the RGB light shows |

AS models keep their position and colour lights and get no I/HI mode or level.
No audio fields, positions or other capabilities are read. Disconnecting clears
these values, and a late reply cannot update the next connection.

### STOP and release behavior

Every held control has a time limit, and its cleanup runs on the link it
started on even if the command is cancelled. P1 sends the STOP for the same
motor or group after its release delay. P2 sends the zero-key release to both
sides, plus the side releases a tap sends. A fresh tap sends seven writes over
six steps; the last step sends the release twice. An interrupted tap keeps its
counter.

STOP sends the motor-stop action once, also during an automatic preset or
memory move. P2 sends it to the selected side; P1 uses its shared motor-stop.
Cancelling a command never suppresses these writes.

On non-split I/HI models, releasing a sonic mode button sends a D0 query
200 ms later. **Position500i does not.** The app's side-toggle queries are not
sent, because the integration has no side picker.

### Vectors

`tests/test_cheerssleep_vectors.py` checks the app's literal frames, the fixed caller expansions, counters and rollover, burst persistence and the parsers. These come from the app, not from captures of a bed.

## Profiles

### CheersSleep profile

**App:** [CheersSleep](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.cheers.sleep) v2.7.0 (40), `com.cheers.sleep`

**Status:** Not yet tested

#### Setup

1. Choose **CheersSleep app**.
2. Choose the model key the app shows. All 36 keys are offered, in setup and in
   Reconfigure. The bed's name and services cannot identify the model.

The model key sets the motors, presets, massage and lights. On a bed with two
receivers, each side keeps its own model.

**Paired and split beds:** a split model added as one bed controls the left
side, as the app does when it opens. Use **Add Left, Right and Both controls**
in Configure to get separate Left and Right devices on the same Bluetooth
address.

Discovery needs the advertised service. The first manufacturer entry, in
numeric order, gives the model key: for ID 89 the key is 89 plus payload byte 2
(signed); for any other ID the ID is the key. Short or unknown records are
ignored. Setup, Reconfigure and imported entries save the chosen key as
`product_type`.

On split models, P1 foot and Flat stay shared by both sides. A timed foot move
for both P1 sides runs once on the receiver for the requested time; back and
lumbar moves run per side. Whether the P2 release stops one side or both
depends on the bed's firmware and still needs testing.

#### Controls

Covers appear only for the model's motors, with timed and held controls
within the integration's hold limits. Presets and memory use the app's command
paths; saves ask for confirmation. Massage buttons, sonic level, RGB light and
massage state sensors appear where the model has them.

| Axis | Cover | Buttons |
|------|-------|---------|
| Storage model `all` | Storage lift | Storage lift up / down |
| Combined back, legs (and lumbar) | | All sections up / down |
| `lift` (both lifts) | Bed lift | Bed lift up / down |
| `lift_head`, `lift_foot` | Head lift, Foot lift | Head lift up / down, Foot lift up / down |

P1 sleep reports name their side, so each side has its own sensors, and a native side device shows only its own: Left/Right in bed and asleep (binary sensors), heart rate, breath rate, snore count and snore power. They are disabled by default. The snore flags, the gatem/gateo fields, the sleep module MAC and the shared control-mode bit are parsed but not exposed. P2 **Refresh bed state** is a diagnostic button, disabled by default, because the integration queries on connect. Split non-RGB models keep it enabled: connect queries one side, so the other side gets light feedback only from this button.

Movement, Flat, memory recall and STOP clear the preset selection, so the next
press of that preset recalls it. A colour-light toggle runs once per receiver,
also when it targets both sides; position-light toggles run per side.

The `adjustable_bed.cheerssleep` action sends the same bed controls and the
extra P1 screens some models offer. `seven_motion` uses the split layout with
an optional `sleeper` field (left or right), which must match the targeted
side. `ten_*` and `newten_*` use the ordinary P1 commands for the selected
position 1 to 4 (all, back, feet, waist), also on split models, with separate
recall and save. `rgb_preview` and `rgb2_preview` wait 200 and 150 ms between
preview frames; RGB2 uses white. A commit waits 10 to 120 ms first and saves
the colour 500 ms later.

P2 light on and off need the light's current state. If the light is already in
the asked state nothing is sent; otherwise the toggle and its release are sent.
With the state unknown, or a toggle still unconfirmed, on and off are refused:
press **Refresh bed state** first. There are no separate P2 on and off frames.

#### State

P1 massage levels are counted by the integration, not reported by the bed.
P2 state comes from the bed's replies. Raw sleep fields keep the bed's values,
with no units added.

A D0 reply updates the light at once. Brightness 0 to 100 % maps to Home
Assistant's 0 to 255; a value outside that range leaves brightness unknown.
Colour and brightness are cleared when the connection ends.

#### Limitations

Wi-Fi and network setup, cloud services, accounts, firmware updates and the
app's audio, phone, desk and seating features are outside this Bluetooth bed
integration. Massage that the bed itself reports is supported.

## Notes

### Analysis provenance

Based on CheersSleep 2.7.0 (`com.cheers.sleep`).
